requirements.requirement: Cron job configured to run /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance daily at 02:15 on node1
requirements.summary: /etc/cron.d/inventory-maintenance created with '15 2 * * * root /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1' (cmd-9a9fd95e1b834f66), crond confirmed active/enabled both before (cmd-6962c27e0cfb4ec5, cmd-11fb9182edfa4a72) and after reboot (cmd-11d9883abb1d4855), and the cron.d file content and permissions were confirmed intact post-restart, showing the schedule persists.

Running the exact cron command line manually (sh -c '/usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1') created and appended to the log file with expected timestamped content (cmd-11fb9182edfa4a72), and the pre-reboot log entry was confirmed to persist after the restart, with a fresh manual run appending a new line afterward (cmd-11d9883abb1d4855).

requirements.requirement: The target script /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance must be a valid, runnable executable producing output (implicit precondition for the cron job to be meaningful)
requirements.summary: The pre-existing file (matching the prepared baseline hash/permissions of root:root:644) contained leftover heredoc/install text rather than a working script (cmd-891f8ddde5fd4941), which would not run correctly under cron. The executor rewrote it as a valid #!/bin/sh script, set 0755 root:root, and verified correct output both immediately (cmd-16d13ab46e0849f6) and post-restart (cmd-11d9883abb1d4855). This mutation was necessary to make the daily cron job produce meaningful output as instructed, rather than an out-of-scope change.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 (pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/config state)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id fb2aa416... with crond active, cron file, script, and log state (cmd-962079384bd54bbf). A backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' returned an acknowledgement (cmd-75874eded6444f54), followed by connection timeouts during the reboot window (cmd-da86e1a7e5234f25, cmd-33a6d438e1cc4ede) and a new boot_id 160e0496... on reconnection (cmd-ebed0952d8314876), independently corroborated by the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot. Post-restart, crond active/enabled, cron.d file, script permissions, and pre-reboot log entry were all confirmed recovered, and the script ran successfully again (cmd-11d9883abb1d4855).

overall_summary: The executor satisfied the core task: a daily 02:15 cron job on node1 runs /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance with output retained in /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log, verified via direct execution of the exact cron command line. It also repaired a pre-existing non-functional script (matching the prepared baseline's broken content) that would otherwise have made the cron job produce no useful output, a defensible action given the task's implicit requirement that the scheduled command actually run. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was fully and coherently demonstrated: baseline boot identity and healthy state, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and full post-restart recovery of crond, the cron config, the script, and the log data.
limitations: The 02:15 daily trigger itself was never observed firing from crond; evidence instead relies on config presence plus manual execution of the identical command line, which is standard but not a live cron-triggered observation.

It cannot be fully determined from available evidence whether the original broken script content was an intentional test fixture or an unintended prepare-stage defect, though either way the executor's repair was necessary for the task to produce meaningful output.

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed mutations map clearly to task requirements or the restart protocol: rewriting the broken pre-existing script (cmd-5d4cd8ae53544609) was necessary since the prepared file contained non-functional leftover heredoc/install text and the task requires the scheduled job to actually run and retain output; creating /etc/cron.d/inventory-maintenance (cmd-9a9fd95e1b834f66) directly satisfies the scheduling requirement; the reboot (cmd-75874eded6444f54) was a bounded, fully-recovered mutation required by the fixed restart-evidence protocol, with post-restart state confirmed intact. No abandoned files, failed services, unnecessary experiments, or weakened security controls were observed in the lifecycle diff (only expected boot-id-tied ephemeral /tmp entries and a reboot.log, with no residual failed-services or package-health degradation).
